claims.claim: Cash does not transfer between islands during the campaign.

citations.review_text: A decent park management sim set the the world of the Jurassic films. Would have liked some more customization with more than the dinos, but you'll also have your hands full enough with just managing the dinosaurs and making sure you have enough cash to manage them that you won't have too much time to fiddle around with the color of your souvenir shops. [b]Quick advice:[/b] [i] cash doesn't transfer between islands, but collected fossils do...[/i] Do with that information what you will.

This right here is the game I wish I could have played as a kid. My love for dinosaurs is still there, but that moment in a boy’s childhood when dinosaurs are everything would have been elevated by this game. I guess we just had to wait for animations and graphics to get better to have a management simulation game based on Jurassic Park.

This game does everything well; it captures you with the nostalgia element, it draws you in with the scenery, and finally, with the overall point of the game: having a dinosaur park.

Would I be lying if I said that every time I released a dino in the park, I wasn’t as excited as a little kid? Just seeing the animation of a T-Rex getting out into the wild is to die for. The fact that you can follow them and see what they do is cool, and it makes for some nice in-game downtime activity.

The gameplay is similar to other management simulation games, the difference being the dinosaurs: creating parks on different islands and completing objectives to unlock new regions where you can discover new fossils. The way the story progresses is just fun; you can take your time with it most of the time, which is cool, because taking care of dinosaurs is not easy. Some of them like to be in a herd, some like to be alone, and you have to cater to their needs.

Another immersive mechanic is that you can drive around the park, you can medicate your sick dinos, and you can take photos of them from the car. That is just pure fun, driving around the park, sometimes hiding, trying not to scare the dinosaurs away, just for that one perfect shot.

Another cool thing: some of the actors from the Jurassic movies are voicing their characters in the game. The biggest surprise was when I heard Jeff Goldblum right at the beginning of the game.

This game is for everyone who loves dinosaurs and wants to recreate Jurassic Park with their own hands. There are so many things to explore that it is better if you find them out by yourself.

claims.claim: The game lacks a pause button during gameplay.

citations.review_text: Might be a bit blinded by nostalgia on this one, but I think it still makes for a fun campaign. Definitely would not recommend if you want to build the dinosaur park of your dreams, or if you want a gripping story, but the campaign does make you feel like some sort of Ingen operative planning miniature Jurassic Worlds, in a weirdly unrealistic but charming kind of way. It does the controlled chaos thing super well, especially on Isla Pena. No pause button means there's real pressure, and you'll have to tranq dinos from your chopper amidst a raging storm, which is really fun honestly. Overall would recommend.
It's a bunch of waiting without the pause/fast forward options in later games, but its an excellent first installment of a great game franchise!

citations.review_text:
I'm a big fan of city building / management and dinosaur games, so JWE definitely scratches that itch that I have to build a dinosaur park that, unlike the movie, doesn't actually go to hell XD

I really love how they tie in so hard to the show, but yet also pivot off into their own alternate timeline where, unlike the movies (JW1 and JW:FK), the parks don't fall apart. In fact, we actually have missions to work on managing successful ones, saving those that are failing, and even carrying out interesting missions that tie into what happens in the shows.

Though that last 1 does lead to some comical moments. For instance, there's a mission to evacuate dinosaurs from the exploding volcano in JW:FK, but in doing so we also build a mini park to generate money for our goals, which is pretty funny. 

Ah yes, please come and take a look at the dinosaurs as we evac them from the island. Don't mind the volcanic ash or the fact that u might die for the impending eruption. 

The amount of content here is really quite staggering, even without all the DLCs. I love how much customisation options we have and its really quite fun to design a diverse park with all sorts of dinosaurs, especially when I get to fit in multiple species together in the same enclosure :)

Challenge mode is also quite fun and interesting, though its also where my 1 gripe is with the game. If u play on max difficulty, too much relies on getting a good set of initial missions because some are just so much better than others when it comes to ease of completion and rewards. I feel that this should be better balance so that u don't keep restarting until u get an "optimal" set to even try on.

Other than that though, this is an awesome game for any city / park management or dinosaur fan, especially if u loved the JW movies.

I'll start by saying that this game is very good. It is very entertaining, fun, and the challenges are genuinely challenging.
However, there are some things to consider before buying.
 - The second game that exists for this game series is better. The story is different, but the game is pretty well the same. They added features to the second game that could've easily been added to this game in an update. But charging people for a new game with very few new features is more profitable. It's important to note that I have only played this game from the game series, not the second, so take this with a grain of salt.
 - If you played Operation Genesis, the Jurassic Park game, there are things you will miss while playing this game. I like the Jurassic Park theming better in the original, and a lot of the herding mechanics are missing from this game.
Overall though, I do recommend this game if you want a cheaper, more base-level, version of the second Jurassic World game. If you have the second game in this series, there's no need to buy this one, and vice versa. If you don't have any of these games and want a good, realistic, dinosaur park game, get Prehistoric Kingdom instead. The only reason to get this game over the other two is that it is finished, polished, and has the movies' lore and theming.
Also, this game is 7 years old and goes on sale often, so definitely wait for a sale before purchasing it.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the path-making tool is poorly designed.

citations.review_text:
The Good
The moment you boot up Jurassic World Evolution, you're handed the keys to literal godhood and the first thing you do is slap a T-Rex back into existence just because you can. The dinosaurs themselves are jaw-droppingly gorgeous—feathers, scales, that glassy dead-eyed stare that makes you question if the devs secretly cloned one in the basement. Watching a pack of Velociraptors sprint across your island while Jeff Goldblum drawls sarcastic life lessons in your ear is peak dopamine. The storms are cinematic chaos: lightning cracking, rain turning paths into rivers, and suddenly your five-star luxury lodge becomes a pteranodon buffet. There's something profoundly satisfying about building a park where profit soars because you let nature (read: murder machines) do what nature does best. That first perfect-genome Indominus Rex hatch? You feel like a mad scientist who just won the evil lottery.

The Bad
The campaign quickly reveals itself as forty hours of corporate busywork disguised as dinosaur theme-park management. You're not running Jurassic World; you're running errands for angry board members who want you to find one specific amber sample with 87% completion or they'll tank your stock price. Guests are the dumbest lifeforms on the planet—happily queuing for the T-Rex exhibit during a category-five hurricane, then one-star reviewing you because the gift shop ran out of plush Compys. The economy swings wildly between "infinite money glitch via spam hatcheries" and "bankrupt because one Triceratops sneezed near the monorail." You spend way too much time micromanaging foliage density and temperature sliders for animals that would happily eat your staff regardless of whether the ferns are 3% too tropical. And the DLC situation is straight-up predatory—you buy the base game, realise half the cool stuff is locked behind season passes, and suddenly you're $80 deep wondering if Frontier just cloned your wallet.

The Ugly
Bugs are the real apex predators her…

ROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAARRRRRRRRRRRR!!! If you ever wanted to be a capitalist fat cat who profits off of the exploitation of extinct animals, this is "right up your alley." I wish it had more options for designing and decorating the park, and the path maker flat out sucks, but it is what is am. I'm also mad that you can't drag-and-drop people into the carnivore pens. BOOO!!! 8.5 out of 10.
